lesson_title: Jack Up a Sandwich, Build the Magaliesberg
hook_text: The Magaliesberg is a sandwich on a car jack. Three clicks, three mountain ranges.
clip_script: Build a sandwich — bread, cheese, bread, ham, bread — and lay it flat. That is the Karoo, flat layers, flat-topped hills. Now prop one end on a matchbox. You just invented a new kind of mountain. Run a finger down the smooth top slice: one long gentle ramp riding a single layer — the dip slope. Look at the cut end where the knife went through, all the layers sawn off in a steep little wall — the scarp slope. Dip follows, scarp cuts. Four words, every diagram labelled. Now slide a car jack under it and lift. Click one, a gentle lean up to about 25 degrees: a cuesta — wheelbarrow ramp with a cliff at the back. Click two, past 25 heading for 45: the ramp turns into a scramble, the ridge sharpens — a homoclinal ridge, and you have driven past the national showpiece, because that is exactly what the Magaliesberg is: a quartzite sandwich jacked to click two, running a hundred kilometres past Pretoria. Click three, past 45 degrees, layers nearly upright — and the ramp vanishes. Both faces steep, crest thin as a blade, spiky as a boar's spine: a hogsback. And the rule underneath it all: the harder the layers lean, the narrower and more even the ridge, until its two faces become twins. One sandwich, three clicks, every leaning ridge in the country named.
visual_style: A real sandwich rising on a car jack in three clicks, each click morphing into a ridge cross-section with its angle and name stamped on, closing on an aerial run down the Magaliesberg crest with the sandwich ghosted beneath it.
mood: Kitchen-table experiment snapping into mountain-range scale.
pacing: Tactile quick start, three crisp beats for the three clicks, glide-out landing on the real ridge.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name every tilted ridge on your next road trip.
